newsitem.title: USA: W.House expresses concern about Israeli move.
newsitem.headline: W.House expresses concern about Israeli move.

text.p: The White House on Wednesday expressed dissatisfaction with Israel's decision to build new Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem.
"The decision taken today further complicates an already complicated situation," said a White House spokesman, David Johnson.

Defying U.S. objections and Palestinian warnings of a wave of violence, Israel on Wednesday approved the building of thousands of new Jewish homes in mainly Arab East Jerusalem. Palestinians saw the move as an attempt to cement Israel's hold over the entire city.
Johnson suggested the move was not in the spirit of cooperation that Israelis and Palestinians used in reaching an accord granting Palestinian rule to the West Bank city of Hebron.
"The United States has been encouraging the parties to take steps which will build further confidence in the peace process following the successful negotiation of the Hebron agreement," he said.
He said the U.S. view had been communicated to the government of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who visited President Bill Clinton at the White House two weeks ago.
